# Result

The cumulative-mass two-pointer reference and an independently constructed
transportation linear program agreed in all **3,362** tested cases.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Total cases | 3,362 |
| Failed cases | 0 |
| Maximum absolute objective discrepancy | \(7.106\times10^{-15}\) |
| Maximum LP marginal residual | \(2.221\times10^{-16}\) |
| Frozen comparison tolerance | \(10^{-10}\) |

This is computational evidence for the finite-grid algorithm identity. It is
not a source-level verification that the resulting covariance is the standard
polytomous Mokken denominator.

# Grid construction

- Support sizes: \(K_x,K_y\in\{2,3,4,5\}\).
- Marginal masses: all weak compositions of denominator four, including zero
  masses, with a deterministic maximum of 12 representative vectors per
  support size.
- Score maps: consecutive integer scores and a deterministic nonconsecutive
  (“gapped”) map.
- Cross-product: every retained \(x\)-mass and \(y\)-mass vector for every
  support-size and score-map combination.
- Case IDs and deterministic integer pseudo-seeds are retained even though
  enumeration uses no random draws.

# Independence of the comparison

`solve-transport-lp.R` constructs one decision variable per coupling cell,
row- and column-marginal equality constraints, nonnegativity constraints and
the score-product objective. It does not call the two-pointer reference.

`two-pointer-reference.R` instead computes intersections of cumulative-mass
intervals. It does not call `lpSolve`. Only input/output comparisons are
shared.

# Retained artifacts

- `../results/exhaustive-grid-summary.csv` contains 32
  support-size-by-score-map summaries.
- `../results/exhaustive-grid-failures.csv` preserves the complete failure
  schema; it contains zero rows for this run.
- `../run-exhaustive-grid.R` deterministically regenerates both files and
  exits nonzero if any case exceeds the frozen tolerance.

# Interpretation boundary

The test grid supports an adversarial review of the proof skeleton, tie
handling and algorithm invariants. Production ordinal support remains closed
because the Phase 3 Molenaar–Rüschendorf–Andreadis source crosswalk is still
`BLOCKED`.
